header.title: Latex Suite 1.13.1 behaviour fixtures

source.refs: Paths in `refs` are relative to the repository root at tag 1.13.1; line numbers refer to that tag.

header.howProduced: Every `after` was produced by running the plugin's own CodeMirror extensions (keymaps, snippet engine, lezer Markdown+LaTeX parser, tabstop state) from the 1.13.1 source in jsdom with DEFAULT_SETTINGS and the default snippets, then reviewed against the source. Nothing was hand-written. Two things Obsidian supplies were emulated (flag `emulated`): whether the caret is inside a fenced code block (closed fence only) or inline code.
header.settings: DEFAULT_SETTINGS (src/settings/settings.ts:97-160). The inline math preview is off (UI only; it changes no text). Tab size 4, indent unit two spaces, multiple selections allowed. No host auto-pairing of brackets or $ (Obsidian's own feature, not Latex Suite's).

notation.|: the caret (an empty selection). With several selections every caret is shown.
notation.«…»: a non-empty selection. In `before` the anchor is at « and the head at »; exact anchor/head for `after` are in `afterState.selection`.
notation.¦: a literal vertical bar in the document (so that | can mean the caret). Replace ¦ with | to get the real text.

fields.input: A string is typed one character per keypress (each character is a separate keydown). One of the names Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Shift+Enter, Backspace is that key. Undo is the editor's undo command. Caret:N moves the caret to offset N of the current document (like a mouse click; used to show how tabstops react to caret moves). An array is applied in order; array items follow the same rules.
fields.after: Document after the last step, with caret/selection marked. When Latex Suite did not handle a printable key, the key was inserted at the caret, replacing any selection — that is the host's default and is included. When it did not handle Tab/Shift+Tab/Enter/Shift+Enter/Backspace, the document is left untouched and `passThrough` names the key: the host's own behaviour for that key applies next (indent, newline, delete…).
fields.afterTabstops: null when no tabstop is active. Otherwise the document (no caret markers) with every active tabstop range marked: ⟨k⟩ is an empty tabstop of group k, ⟨k:text⟩ a tabstop of group k covering `text`. Groups are numbered 0…n-1 after normalisation; the same k appearing several times is one group with several ranges (they are selected together).
fields.tabstopIndex: The current group (the one the caret is in); null when none is active. Tab goes to index+1, Shift+Tab to index-1.
fields.handled: One boolean per step: true when Latex Suite consumed that keypress (snippet, autofraction, tabout, matrix shortcut, tabstop jump, auto-delete of $). For Undo: whether anything was undone. For Caret:N: always true.
fields.beforeState: Exact initial state: document and selection offsets (UTF-16 code units, as in JavaScript).
fields.afterState: Exact final state: document, every selection range {anchor, head}, and the active tabstop groups as offset pairs [from, to] plus the current index.
fields.id: Stable identifier LS001…; the order follows the feature groups of spec.md. LS251 onwards (flag `added`) were recorded the same way for the Swift port: math detection around Markdown constructs, UTF-16 outside the BMP, typing inside tabstops, several carets, retyping an environment name.
fields.flags: quirk = the 1.13.1 behaviour looks unintended (reproduce it only if you want bug-for-bug parity); emulated = depends on Obsidian's own code/code-block detection, which the harness reproduced from the rule in src/editor_context/context.ts; host = the final key was passed through to the host editor. added = recorded after the first 250, for the Swift port. added = recorded after the first 250, for the Swift port. added = recorded after the first 250, for the Swift port.
